en: The Sūtra on the Girl Yaśodharā, spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, of Great Wisdom, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling in the kingdom of Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At the Jeta Grove,
together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
as well as immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
As well as the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, all came to assemble.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"I recall that in the past,
while dwelling to the north of the Snowy Mountains, I traveled to Mount Gandhamādana."
He saw a young girl,
her body adorned with the marks and signs of a hundred blessings;
she wore a garment of deer skin and used various venomous snakes as her necklace.
They are constantly surrounded by various venomous insects,
such as vipers and adders, with whom they play and frolic;
they drink poisonous nectar and eat poisonous fruits.
Seeing me, she said, "Virtuous one,
you should know and listen as I proclaim the mantra of Śaṅkhinī,
which can eliminate all poisons in the world."
If anyone hears this mantra and upholds my name,
they shall not be harmed by any poisons whatsoever.
At that time, the young girl expounded it for me.
Having heard it from her,
I have constantly upheld this Dharma to benefit sentient beings.
I shall now declare the mantra:
*tadyathā oṃ irimeḍe tirimeḍe iridirimide nūbhe nūbham*.
1. Āli āye (ā and ye in the level tone) 2. Nṛce nṛcaḥ (nṛce and nṛcaḥ with the departing tone on the final syllable) 3.
Āli āye (ā and ye in the level tone) 4. Dekaraṇi (de-karaṇi, with the *ch* sound [presentī] applied to the *ni*) 5.
Vākaraṇi (vā-karaṇi, with the departing tone on the *ni*, same as above) 6. Kaśmiri (kaśmi-ri, with the long vowel drawn out) 7. Kaśmirā-mukte (kaśmirā-mukte)
2. *dvika* (two combined) 3. *āṅga* 4. *aṅgī* (with the *ji* and *zhi* initials combined) 5. *aṅgane* (the *ga* is departing tone) 6.
*aṅganā* (the *ga* is departing tone) 7. *ekaline* 8. *elī elī* (the first *li* is drawn out) 9. *elīye* (the *yi* is level tone) 10.
*ākāyāye* (the *ka* is departing tone and the *ya* is drawn out; the *ye* is level tone) 11. *ambāve* (the *ba* is drawn out)
16. Śviti (dissyllabic) tiḥ; 17. Śviti (dissyllabic) tado nne;
18. Ānanu bira kṣe svāhā. 19. The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
If a person hears this dhāraṇī in its entirety,
they will remain free from all poisons for seven years thereafter;
if they constantly uphold it, [the same shall hold true].
No venomous insects or any poisonous drugs whatsoever shall be able to harm them.
Should any venomous snake come to bite such a person,
its head shall split into seven pieces, just like the stalks of a *laṅkha* plant.
Whoever receives and maintains this mantra-dharma should first make offerings of white substances to the teacher;
thereafter, by receiving and maintaining it, one will certainly attain accomplishment.
"O bhikṣus, you should know:
do not recite this mantra in the presence of a snake;
the snake will surely die."
One should use this mantra to empower a dead snake so that it may be restored to life.
The mantra is as follows:
1. *Rūṇḍe* 2. *Tiṭṭhe* (same as before) 3.
*Phuṭṭhara-khe* 4. *Phuṭṭhara-khe* 5. *Phuṭṭhaṇa-ṇara-khe* 6. *Sapphara-khe* 7.
*Sapphaṭṭhaṇa-ṇara-khe* 8. *Nāgara-khe* 9. *Nāgaṭṭha*
Namaḥ (as before) nara-khe ā-ci-ca-le kīla-viśe ṣṭi-te ṣṭi-tāva-ni manda-ri i-li-ri he-ri he-ri dande.
*Da-nai-ying* (20) *tadṛhe* (21) *sphoṭa sphoṭa svāhā* (22).
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this dhāraṇī, [remained silent].
He addressed the bhikṣus:
"This mantra of mine can neutralize all poisons in the world;
it cannot be harmed by insect venom, demonic possession, sorcery, medicinal toxins, or the like."
If there are those who have been poisoned,
by empowering them with this mantra, all [poison] shall be eliminated.
O bhikṣus, this is the Yaṅguli-dhāraṇī.
It was spoken within the great assembly of all Tathāgatas.
It is a word that is true, not false, and not inverted;
it is a word as it is, not otherwise. For all poisons of medicine, poisons of spells, poisons of insects, and poisons of malevolent spirits—
If they wish to come and cause harm,
one can cause them to return to that which was originally given to them,
making all their poisons enter into water, fire, pillars, and walls.
It also causes them to enter the stages;
it prevents all poisons from becoming toxic and is able to completely eliminate them.
If a person upholds this sutra and recites it once daily,
it will not only eliminate all worldly poisons,
but will also be able to eradicate the three poisons within their own body.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke the随心 (suixin) mantra and the method for accomplishment of the maiden Śaṅkhinī.
If a practitioner desires to accomplish this rite:
First, one must abstain from the five pungent vegetables, as well as salt and oil.
One should cease speech and remain in a pure place,
bathing three times a day and changing clothes three times a day.
If one forms the mudrā and recites the随心真言 (Sui-xin zhen-yán / *Cittavajra-mantra*) ten thousand times, the practice will be accomplished.
Furthermore, when performing any task, one will certainly attain success. The随心真言 is as follows: [Mantra].

Oṃ asi-heruka śūla-herukāyudha gṛ-sa-gṛ-sa jvala-jvala mahākāli mahāyogini śvare Oṃ phaṭ pūṭara-he svāhā Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Now I shall further explain the *yaṅguli* mudrā and the method of meditative practice (*vipaśyanā*).
As for its fundamental mudrā:
clasp the two hands together as if holding an object,
with the two little fingers joined side by side.
The remaining eight fingers are each slightly spread apart and bent to form [the mudrā].
Having bound this seal, recite the aforementioned root mantra and empower the five places of one's own body.
This refers to the mudrās for dispersing [the deities] upon the right shoulder, left shoulder, heart, throat, forehead, and the crown of the head.
Next, bind the *cittānugā-mudrā* (the mudrā following the mind) by spreading the five fingers of the right hand.
Slightly bending [the fingers] into the shape of a lion’s claws, the seal is thus formed.
Having bound this seal, recite the随心真言 (Sui-xin zhen-yán) seven times to empower the five places.
Once the practitioner has performed the preliminary rites for accomplishment, [proceed].
When performing the rite for the removal of poison,
visualize yourself as the maiden Śāṅkhinī,
green in color and resembling a nāga girl in form.
He is endowed with seven heads and possesses a halo;
one should visualize him as having four arms:
the first right hand holds a trident, and the second hand holds five peacock feathers.
The first left hand holds a black snake, and the second hand bestows fearlessness (*abhaya-mudrā*).
One should further visualize her body adorned with necklaces, earrings, bracelets, and anklets made of the seven precious gems.
Furthermore, one uses various snakes as ornaments for the necklace.
One visualizes flames streaming forth from every single pore.
Having performed this visualization, [one stands] before the person who has been bitten.
Form the root mudrā and the随心印 (anucitta-mudrā),
consecrate the five places of one’s own body,
and take a bowl of refined copper and fill it with water.
Recite the随心真言 (Svāhṛdaya-mantra) seven times to empower it.
With the right hand, scoop up water and strike the heart of the person who has been stung;
all poisonous vapors will gradually be eliminated.
Then, insert this phrase into the mantra syllables:
*zla saḥ haḥ viśoka saḥ haḥ*. Thereupon, take up pure earth and empower it seven times.
It shall surround the person who has been stung on all sides,
and all poisons will be extinguished at that very moment.
Furthermore, another method is to [place it] before the person who has been stung.
Forming the root mudrā, recite the single-syllable mantra *HŪṂ* many times,
or empower [the area] by reciting the single-syllable mantra *PHUṬ*; in either case,
one will be able to eliminate all poisons.
If one constantly upholds this Rāgūri rite,
it can extinguish all poisons in the world;
whatever is sought shall not fail to accord with one's heart's desire.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra,
the great assembly— consisting of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and others— hearing what the Buddha had spoken,
all rejoiced greatly, accepted it with faith, and practiced accordingly.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Maiden Yaṅguli (Rāṅguli)
